task.description:
HARD GATE on CODE-DESIGNER's POST-GATE AMENDMENT to ISS-0119's design -- new §13 at line 1060 of `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md`, plus a banner under the title and cross-reference markers on §5, A4 and A5, committed at 6c999e4.

WHY THIS EXISTS. You passed §§1-12 on re-gate pass 3. Then TEST-DESIGNER implemented assertion A4 and RAN it for the first time, and it went red on three previously undeclared entries in FROZEN volume 1: line 4803 REQ-053 (no `note:`), line 4896/4899 REQ-056 (`timestamp:` instead of `at:`), line 5050 REQ-054 (no `note:`). Real drift -- ORCH corroborated by field-count arithmetic and CODE-DESIGNER re-corroborated with anchored patterns (182 req/event/agent, 181 at, 180 note, one `^    timestamp: ` at line 4899). TEST-DESIGNER refused to weaken A4 to clear the red, which is why an amendment exists rather than a quiet edit. §13 is NEW design and has NOT been validated by anyone. Gate it as you gated the original.

SCOPE: gate §13 and the amendment's cross-reference markers. §§1-12 are already gated -- do NOT re-derive them, EXCEPT to verify the amendment did not disturb them (see check 1).

CHECKS, each with its own recorded verdict:

1. NOTHING ELSE MOVED. CODE-DESIGNER claims §§1-12 are 'otherwise byte-unchanged' apart from the banner and three cross-reference markers. Verify with `git show 6c999e4` / `git diff` that the change is additive and confined to §13 plus those markers, and that §8's erratum, the freeze-and-roll shape, the header text and the 23 instruction sites were not revisited. Also confirm the commit touched only the artefact and the handoff.

2. THE CHOICE IS SOUND. Candidate (i) was chosen: a top-level `known_shape_anomalies:` key, keyed {path, entry_line, req, event, kind, field, found_as, found_line, should_have_been, cause}, with A4 splitting into A4a (vocabulary) and A4b (shape). Judge the reasoning on its merits, not its confidence. The central claim to test: does (i) genuinely NOT WEAKEN A4? CODE-DESIGNER argues it strengthens it, because the shape rule still applies to every volume, the three stop being red by being DECLARED rather than by ceasing to be checked, and bidirectional set equality newly makes a silent 'cleanup' of one of them FAIL -- something A4 could not detect before. Verify that bidirectionality is actually specified in §13.5 and not merely asserted in prose.

3. THE EXCEPTION LIST CANNOT GROW SILENTLY. The claim is that the list is bounded and permanent by construction because volume 1 is frozen and digest-pinned. Test the other half: what stops a future agent from making a NEW shape violation acceptable by simply adding a record to `known_shape_anomalies:`? The vocabulary mechanism has the same theoretical hole. If the design has no answer, that is worth a finding at MAJOR -- a declare-to-silence mechanism with no friction is a gate an agent can satisfy by editing what it measures, which core-directives.md forbids outright.

4. VISIBILITY, THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ORCH SET. The three entries must remain visible where a reader LANDS, not merely be technically recorded. §13 claims four places: the index's `known_shape_anomalies:`, the current volume's header via §13.8's addendum, `mix test` output whenever A4b fails, and §13.1's table. Verify each claim is actually specified -- particularly that §13.8 gives verbatim header text and that A4b's failure output really does name all three.

5. A5 IS UNTOUCHED AND DISJOINT. §13 claims A5 keeps the same text, behaviour and same three vocabulary anomalies (3490/3577/3744, field `event`, value SCOPE-CHANGE), must NOT read `known_shape_anomalies:`, and is arithmetically unaffected because the three shape-anomalous entries carry legal vocabulary (req REQ-053/056/054, event `started`) so they never enter A5's on-disk set. VERIFY THE DISJOINTNESS ON THE REAL DATA rather than accepting the argument -- read those entries.

6. THE DIGEST DOES NOT MOVE. §13.7 states frozen_prefix_sha256 is unchanged because the amendment writes zero bytes into `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` -- neither the prefix nor the footer -- and the digest never covered the index. Confirm the amendment truly requires no edit to volume 1, and that A6 therefore stays green with no index change to the digest field.

7. APPLICABLE WITHOUT INVENTION. §13.4 (verbatim index YAML), §13.8 (verbatim volume-header addendum), §13.5 (A4a/A4b behaviour, the four `kind:` values, the misnamed_field-is-ONE-violation rule, the {path, entry_line, kind, field, found_as} identity key, the req/event cross-check, the preserved ISO-8601 parse at line 4899) and §13.7 (two signature-only additions to test/support/status_history.ex) must be executable as written. Judge whether ELIXIR-DEV and TEST-DESIGNER could apply them without inventing anything. Check §13.4's YAML is well-formed and its three records match the ACTUAL on-disk entries -- line numbers, req ids, events and the `timestamp:`-vs-`at:` detail.

8. A8 CLAUSE (c). A8 gains a clause requiring the current volume's header to contain the literal token `known_shape_anomalies:`, so a volume opened by copy cannot silently drop the declaration at roll time. Judge whether that actually closes the roll-time hole.

9. THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS in §13.11 -- whether `note:` is genuinely mandatory or only conventional, and whether `known_anomalies:` should be renamed. Confirm neither hides a decision the applying agents would have to invent. The first is load-bearing: if `note:` is only conventional, then two of the three 'anomalies' are not anomalies at all and the correct fix is to A4's rule rather than to the exception list. State your own view.

10. NO IMPLEMENTATION LEAKED IN. §13 should be signatures, YAML content and specified behaviour -- not written test code.

SCHEMA NOTE, for your record and already corrected by ORCH's request to CODE-DESIGNER: step-04d's handoff was completed with `result.status: "SUCCESS"`, which is not one of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's five legal values. Confirm it now reads PASS when you read that file; if it still says SUCCESS, note it as MINOR.

PASS only if every check passes. On FAIL, name each gap with its specific missing element. Do not fix the design yourself and do not edit the artefact.
acceptance_criteria: The verdict is derived from §13 of the artefact itself, and result.summary names what was read
Check 1 verifies via git that the amendment is additive and confined to §13 plus the banner and cross-reference markers
Check 2 states whether candidate (i) genuinely does not weaken A4, and confirms bidirectional set equality is specified in §13.5 rather than only claimed in prose
Check 3 states what, if anything, stops a future agent from silencing a new violation by adding a record, and raises it at MAJOR if there is no answer
Check 4 verifies each of the four claimed visibility surfaces is actually specified, including §13.8's verbatim header text
Check 5 verifies A5's disjointness against the real on-disk entries, not from the argument
Check 6 confirms no edit to volume 1 is required and A6 stays green
Check 7 confirms §13.4's YAML is well-formed and its three records match the actual on-disk entries by line, req, event and field detail
Checks 8, 9 and 10 each carry a recorded verdict, including the validator's own view on whether note: is mandatory or conventional
A per-item verdict is recorded for all 10 checks
The design artefact is not modified by this step

result.summary:
HARD GATE on CODE-DESIGNER's post-gate amendment (§13 of lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md, commit 6c999e4). VERDICT: FAIL on one check of ten (check 3, MAJOR). Checks 1,2,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 PASS. READ, first-hand, not from any producer summary: §13 in full (artefact lines 1060-1400) plus the banner and the §5/A4/A5 markers; `git show --stat 6c999e4` and the full `git show 6c999e4` diff of the artefact; `git diff 6c999e4 HEAD`; docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml in full; docs/status/requirement_status.yaml lines 3488-3493, 3575-3580, 3742-3747, 4799-4812, 4894-4906, 5046-5058 and its header (1-45) and closure footer; docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml lines 1-100; §7's A6/A7/A8 text (artefact 548-575); test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs (A4 block) and test/support/status_history.ex signatures; handoffs/WF03-ISS0119-20260821/step-04d-code-designer-amendment.json. Independent re-derivation: I wrote my own field-set scan of volume 1 (entry = '^  - req: ' line, fields = '^    <name>: ') and it reports 182 entries and EXACTLY three non-conforming ones -- 4803 [event,agent,at], 4896 [event,agent,timestamp,note], 5050 [event,agent,at] -- no fourth, no extra_field, no field_order. §13.4's three records match that scan exactly, and I parsed §13.4's YAML block with a real YAML loader (well-formed, three records, keys as specified).

PER-CHECK VERDICTS.
1. NOTHING ELSE MOVED -- PASS. `git show --stat 6c999e4` = 2 files only (the artefact +362/-3, and step-04d's handoff). The artefact diff is exactly four hunks: @@ -8 (the banner), @@ -404 (§5 cross-reference marker), @@ -518 (markers on A4 and A5; the three '-' lines are the A4/A5 bullets re-emitted with the markers, substance preserved), @@ -1042 (§13, purely additive at EOF). No other line moved: §8's erratum, the freeze-and-roll shape, the header text and the 23 instruction sites are byte-unchanged. `git diff 6c999e4 HEAD` on the artefact = 0 lines, so nothing edited it afterwards, and this step did not modify it either.
2. CANDIDATE (i) DOES NOT WEAKEN A4 -- PASS. The shape rule still runs on every volume, closed and current (§13.5's closing sentence states this explicitly; §13.3 gives the reasoning for rejecting (ii)). The three stop being red by being DECLARED, not by ceasing to be checked. Bidirectionality is genuinely SPECIFIED, not merely asserted in prose: §13.5's A4b carries 'the set of shape violations found on disk equals the index's known_shape_anomalies: set EXACTLY, in both directions', names both failure directions (a new violation fails; a missing one fails = a past entry was silently normalized), and pins the comparison with an explicit identity key {path, entry_line, kind, field, found_as} plus a req/event cross-check against the entry actually at entry_line, plus the preserved ISO-8601 parse at found_line: for the 'field: at' record. That is strictly more detection than pre-amendment A4 had.
3. THE EXCEPTION LIST CANNOT GROW SILENTLY -- FAIL (MAJOR-1). §13.3 claims the list is 'bounded and permanent, not a growing suppression list' on two grounds: volume 1 is frozen and digest-pinned, and volumes 2 onward are 'checked live from their first entry, so a defect there is caught while the volume is still current and appendable'. The first ground is sound. The SECOND ground is exactly the answer this check asks for -- and it is prose only. Nothing in §13.4, §13.5 or §13.7 stops a future agent from appending a malformed entry to the CURRENT volume and then adding a matching known_shape_anomalies: record, at which point A4b is green again and the defect is permanent. The only barriers are §13.10's written instruction ('Do not hand-tune the declared list to make A4b green') and core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures'. Under this project's own weak-model-tolerance rule (core-directives.md, Humanless operation: 'every gate below has a checklist instead of "use good judgement"'), a prose prohibition is not the guard this needs when a mechanical one costs one clause and follows directly from §13.3's own argument. MISSING ELEMENT, named precisely: A4b must additionally assert that every known_shape_anomalies: record's path: names a volume whose index entry has 'status: closed' AND carries a frozen_prefix_sha256: -- i.e. a record may never cite the current volume. That makes 'bounded by construction' machine-enforced instead of claimed, and it changes nothing about the three records now proposed (all cite volume 1, closed, digest-pinned). It also makes the correct route the only route: a shape defect in the current volume must be fixed in the working tree before it is committed, which is what §13.3 already says happens. The same theoretical hole exists in known_anomalies:/A5 today; that is not a reason to reproduce it in new design, and closing it there is out of this amendment's scope (see MINOR-3).
4. VISIBILITY -- PASS, with MINOR-2. Four surfaces claimed in §13.9, checked one at a time: (a) index -- specified verbatim in §13.4, all three records with cause:, and I confirmed the insertion point ('after the existing known_anomalies: block, at top level') is unambiguous against the real index file; (b) current volume's header -- §13.8 gives VERBATIM text in a fenced block (nine comment lines naming 4803/REQ-053, 5050/REQ-054, 4896/REQ-056, the index key, the leave-as-written rule and the A4b consequence), with a real insertion point that exists on disk: docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml:60, the '-- ENTRY SHAPE --' block; (c) §13.1's table in this artefact -- present, with req, event and defect per row; (d) `mix test` -- present but failure-only by construction, and §13.5 does not specify what A4b's failure message must contain (see MINOR-2). Three of the four are always-on, which meets ORCH's binding constraint that a reader LANDS on them.
5. A5 DISJOINTNESS -- PASS, verified on the real data, not from the argument. I read the three vocabulary entries: 3489/3490 REQ-031 'event: SCOPE-CHANGE', 3576/3577 REQ-042, 3743/3744 REQ-038 -- all field: event, value: SCOPE-CHANGE, matching the index's three known_anomalies: records by line (the index keys the FIELD line, 3490/3577/3744; §13.4 keys the ENTRY line for shape records -- two different, internally consistent conventions, each documented in its own block). I read the three shape entries: all carry req: REQ-053 / REQ-056 / REQ-054 and event: started, all legal vocabulary, so none of them enters A5's on-disk set and A5's verdict is arithmetically unaffected. The two sets share no entry. §13.6 states A5's text and behaviour are unchanged and that A5 must not read known_shape_anomalies:; §13.7 confirms anomalies/3 is unchanged and must not start reporting shape violations.
6. THE DIGEST DOES NOT MOVE -- PASS. §13.3 explicitly rejects the sub-option of also writing the three into volume 1's closure footer, so the amendment writes zero bytes into docs/status/requirement_status.yaml -- neither inside frozen_prefix_lines: 5766 nor past it. Every applied change lands in the index (a new top-level key) and in v2's header. The digest covers volume 1's prefix only and never covered the index, so A6 stays green with no edit to frozen_prefix_sha256: 5a1a64ab...804 and no edit to frozen_prefix_lines/entries/lines/bytes_working_tree/roll_rule. Confirmed against the real index file: those fields exist with the values §13.4 quotes.
7. APPLICABLE WITHOUT INVENTION -- PASS. §13.4's YAML parses cleanly under a real YAML loader (I ran it): one top-level key, three mapping records, found_as: null / found_line: null load as null, the folded cause: scalars are valid, and should_have_been: 'at: "2026-08-19T02:40:35Z"' is correctly quoted so the embedded colon does not break the mapping. All three records match the ACTUAL on-disk entries: 4803 is '  - req: REQ-053' with event started and fields [event, agent, at] -- no note:; 4896 is '  - req: REQ-056' with event started and fields [event, agent, timestamp, note], and line 4899 is '    timestamp: "2026-08-19T02:40:35Z"' -- so field: at, found_as: timestamp, found_line: 4899 and the quoted should_have_been value are all exactly right; 5050 is '  - req: REQ-054' with event started and fields [event, agent, at] -- no note:. §13.5's four kind: values, the misnamed_field-is-ONE-violation rule, the identity key, the req/event cross-check and the preserved ISO-8601 parse are all stated as behaviour an implementer can code directly; §13.7's two additions to test/support/status_history.ex are signature-only and path-parameterised ('it must not know the index exists'), consistent with the module's existing shape (entries/1, anomalies/3, measure/1 all take a path). §13.8 is verbatim text with a real anchor. §13.10 assigns each part to a named role. ELIXIR-DEV/DOC-UPDATER and TEST-DESIGNER can apply this without inventing anything.
8. A8 CLAUSE (c) -- PASS, with MINOR-2b. It does close the hole it targets: headers propagate to future volumes by copy, and requiring the literal token known_shape_anomalies: in the current volume's header makes a copy that drops the declaration FAIL rather than quietly shrinking the declaration surface -- the same mechanism A8(a)/(b) already use for the six event values and the two ceilings, so it is idiom-consistent. Its limit, recorded rather than treated as a failure: a header that keeps the token but drops the three line citations still passes clause (c).
9. THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS -- PASS; neither hides a decision the applying agents would have to invent, because §13.4/§13.5/§13.8 fully specify the behaviour under the mandatory reading and Q2 is explicitly not proposed. MY OWN VIEW ON Q1, since it is load-bearing: note: IS mandatory, and the exception list is the correct fix -- not a change to A4's rule. Evidence I checked directly rather than reasoning from the amendment: volume 1's OWN header, in force on 2026-08-19 when these two entries were written, already documents the five-field entry shape with 'note: short free-text (what shipped, or what's blocking)' as the fifth field (docs/status/requirement_status.yaml lines 12-17); volume 2's header states it in mandatory words -- 'ENTRY SHAPE -- all five fields, in this order, every time' (v2.yaml:60); and 180 of 182 entries carry it. So the field was documented, not merely conventional, at the time of the violation, and the two entries are genuine drift. The one fair concession to the question is a wording one, not a rule one: v1's header phrased the shape as a template rather than using the word 'required', which is precisely what §13.4's cause: records ('no mechanical check on entry shape existed at the time'). Weakening A4b to make note: optional would retire a rule 98.9 percent of the corpus follows in order to accommodate two entries -- the attrition §13.11 itself warns against.
10. NO IMPLEMENTATION LEAKED IN -- PASS. §13 contains three fenced blocks and none is Elixir: shell grep invocations used as corroborating evidence in §13.1, the index YAML in §13.4, and the verbatim header comment text in §13.8. §13.5 is specified behaviour; §13.7's two module additions are signatures and return-map shapes only. No test code, no function bodies.
SCHEMA NOTE -- clear. step-04d's handoff now reads result.status: "PASS" (corrected in commit 5bc5882, after 6c999e4). No MINOR raised.
SCOPE DISCIPLINE: §§1-12 were not re-derived, only checked for disturbance per check 1. The design artefact was not modified by this step.

issues.summary: §13's bounding claim for known_shape_anomalies: is prose only -- nothing mechanically stops a future agent from declaring away a NEW shape defect in the CURRENT volume.
issues.detail: §13.3 claims the list is 'bounded and permanent, not a growing suppression list' because volume 1 is frozen and because 'volumes 2 onward are checked live from their first entry, so a defect there is caught while the volume is still current and appendable'. A4b as specified in §13.5 asserts only set equality between on-disk shape violations and the declared list -- it places no constraint on WHICH volume a declared record may cite. An agent that appends a malformed entry to the current volume and adds a matching known_shape_anomalies: record turns A4b green, permanently, with no gate tripped. §13.10's 'Do not hand-tune the declared list to make A4b green' and core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' are the only barriers, and both are prose addressed to an agent's judgement -- which core-directives.md's Humanless-operation section says explicitly must not be what a gate rests on.
issues.missing_element: A4b must additionally assert: every known_shape_anomalies: record's path: names a volume whose index entry has 'status: closed' and carries a frozen_prefix_sha256:. Equivalently: no record may cite the current volume. State it in §13.5 alongside the identity key and the req/event cross-check, and add the corresponding sentence to §13.4's block comment (which currently justifies entry_line stability by volume 1's frozen-ness without making that a rule). This changes none of the three proposed records -- all cite volume 1, closed and digest-pinned -- and makes §13.3's own argument machine-enforced.
issues.action: Return to CODE-DESIGNER for a narrow §13-only amendment.

issues.summary: §13.9 claims 'A4b names all three whenever it fails in either direction', but §13.5 does not specify A4b's failure-message content.
issues.detail: A set-equality failure need only report the symmetric difference, not the full declared set. §13.10 ('Run A4b, read the full set it reports') assumes a full-set report, and the current A4 implementation in test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs already interpolates whole violation lists into its assert message -- so this is very likely to come out right, but it is claimed as a visibility surface without being specified. One sentence in §13.5 requiring the failure message to print BOTH the full on-disk shape-violation set and the full declared set (not just the difference) makes §13.9's claim true by specification.

issues.summary: A8 clause (c) asserts only the literal token, so a header that keeps known_shape_anomalies: while dropping the three line citations still passes.
issues.detail: Clause (c) closes the hole it was written for (a copied header that drops the declaration entirely). Consider strengthening it the way A8(b) treats the ceilings: assert that each entry_line in the index's known_shape_anomalies: appears in the current volume's header text, so the header addendum is a machine-checked copy rather than a prose one. Optional; recorded so the asymmetry with A8(b) is on record rather than a surprise.
issues.action: CODE-DESIGNER's discretion; not required to clear this gate.

issues.summary: known_anomalies:/A5 carries the same declare-to-silence hole as MAJOR-1, and §13.3 cites that parity as support.
issues.detail: §13.3 argues (i) is safe partly because it mirrors known_anomalies:, 'and it has been uncontroversial'. The vocabulary mechanism has never been constrained to closed volumes either. Out of scope for this amendment -- flagged so it is not treated as settled by the parity argument, and so a later run can apply the MAJOR-1 constraint to A5 as well.
issues.action: File/forward for a later run; do not expand this amendment's scope.

result.next_action: ORCH: route back to CODE-DESIGNER for a narrow §13-only re-amendment addressing MAJOR-1 (required) and MINOR-2 (recommended, one sentence); MINOR-2b is discretionary and MINOR-3 is out of scope for this run. §§1-12 are gated and must not be revisited. Re-gate here on §13 only; checks 1,2,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 of this pass need not be re-derived unless §13 changes outside the named elements.
